A parallel Fortran framework for neural networks and deep learning

. It builds a network with three inputs, five hidden units, and two outputs, then trains it on one fixed pair of vectors for 500 steps of stochastic gradient descent. The target is small enough that the run can be read by eye.

program simple
  use nf, only: dense, input, network, sgd
  implicit none
  type(network) :: net
  real, allocatable :: x(:), y(:)
  integer, parameter :: num_iterations = 500
  integer :: n

  print '("Simple")'
  print '(60("="))'

  net = network([ &
    input(3), &
    dense(5), &
    dense(2) &
  ])

  call net % print_info()
only stores the width of the input. It has no weights. Each
call that omits an activation uses the library default, which is the logistic sigmoid. The run prints that name.

children.value: The loop index starts at 0, so the first printed line is the prediction after one update, and the last line is after 501 updates. Every 50 steps the program prints
rather than the loss. By step 450 both outputs match the target at the six decimals in the format, and step 500 repeats that match.

program simple
  use nf, only: dense, input, network, sgd
  implicit none
  type(network) :: net
  real, allocatable :: x(:), y(:)
  integer, parameter :: num_iterations = 500
  integer :: n

  print '("Simple")'
  print '(60("="))'

  net = network([ &
    input(3), &
    dense(5), &
    dense(2) &
  ])

  call net % print_info()

  x = [0.2, 0.4, 0.6]
  y = [0.123456, 0.246802]

  do n = 0, num_iterations

    call net % forward(x)
    call net % backward(y)
    call net % update(optimizer=sgd(learning_rate=1.))

    if (mod(n, 50) == 0) &
      print '(i4,2(3x,f8.6))', n, net % predict(x)

  end do

end program simple
The package file below builds this source with fpm. The Fortran program itself is the file from the repository.

name = "Section_Examples_Simple"

[build]
auto-executables = true
auto-tests = true
auto-examples = true

[install]
library = false

[dependencies]
neural-fortran = { git = "https://github.com/modern-fortran/neural-fortran.git" }

[[executable]]
name = "Section_Examples_Simple"
source-dir = "app"
main = "simple.f90"
